Sources: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000950170-25-021814) and the April 2025 annual-meeting proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-25-100720, filed April 28, 2025), read on EDGAR; the January 2025 special-meeting proxy was not used. LEADER: the proxy gives Saylor 99.9% of Class B and 44.1% of total voting power, but no percentage of all common shares, so pctEconomic is null and the economic share is in leader.derived (7.42%). The proxy's 7.4% 'Beneficial Ownership of Class A Stock (% of Class)' is on an as-converted basis and matches. His total includes 378,500 Class A shares held by a charitable foundation of which he is sole trustee and in which he disclaims beneficial ownership; the proxy counts them as beneficially owned, and so does the derived figure. The derived figure excludes the non-voting perpetual preferred stock, which was first issued in 2025. HOLDERS left empty: the proxy gives the other 5% holders only as a percentage of Class A (Vanguard 6.5%, as of December 31, 2024; BlackRock 5.7%, as of March 31, 2025; Capital International Investors 5.1%, as of December 31, 2024), not of all common stock, so they are omitted rather than converted. BUYBACKS: the FY2024 cash-flow statement has no line for repurchases of common stock; the company was a net issuer (over $16 billion of common stock sold). DIVIDENDS: none on common stock; preferred dividends started only in 2025. Stock comp and geography are small: geography is given to three decimals because two-decimal rounding of $0.26/0.16/0.05 billion would not add up to the $0.46 billion total.
